title: Vehicle/Equipment Access Permit
name: Vehicle/Equipment Access Permit
description: Permit for controlled access and movement of vehicles or mobile equipment in a site area, covering operator competence, route suitability, pedestrian segregation, reversing, loading and parking controls.

fields.label: Driver / Operator Authorisation or Competence Reference
Vehicle Dimensions / Weight / Load Restrictions (if relevant)
Traffic Management Plan / Logistics Plan Reference

sections.title: VEHICLE, EQUIPMENT AND OPERATOR READINESS
items: The vehicle / equipment is suitable for the intended site task and route
The driver / operator is authorised and competent for the vehicle or equipment
Required pre-use checks have been completed with no safety-critical defects outstanding
Brakes, steering, tyres / tracks, lights, mirrors, cameras and warning devices are serviceable as applicable
The load is secure and within the vehicle / route limits
The driver has received the relevant site traffic and access rules

sections.title: ROUTE, GROUND AND SITE SUITABILITY
items: Vehicle and pedestrian routes have been planned to keep people and vehicles apart where possible
The route has adequate width, height, turning space and visibility for the vehicle and load
Ground, haul-road, slab or working-platform capacity is suitable for the intended vehicle / equipment
Overhead services, structures, edges, excavations and other clearance hazards have been assessed
Crossing points, gates, doors and blind corners are controlled where required
Lighting and route condition are adequate for the planned movement

fields.label: Ground / Slab / Working Platform Suitability Reference

sections.title: MOVEMENT, REVERSING AND SIGNALLING
items: Vehicle movements and the need for reversing have been minimised
A one-way or drive-through route is used where reasonably practicable
Reversing areas are controlled so non-essential pedestrians are kept out
A trained and authorised signaller / marshaller is used only where the risk assessment requires one
Driver and signaller have agreed the signalling / communication method where a signaller is used
The driver will stop immediately if visibility is inadequate or the signaller is lost from view

sections.title: LOADING, UNLOADING, PARKING AND ISOLATION
items: Loading / unloading will take place in a designated safe area
People are excluded from crush, trapping and load-fall zones during loading / unloading
The vehicle / equipment will be parked on suitable ground and secured against unintended movement
Parking will not block pedestrian routes, emergency routes or visibility
Vehicle / equipment isolation is defined before people work on, under or around it
Keys, parking brakes, chocks, stabilisers or other controls are used where required

fields.label: Loading / Unloading Exclusion and Control Measures

sections.title: ENVIRONMENTAL, EMERGENCY AND INTERFACE CONTROLS
items: Public-road, delivery, crane, lifting or other simultaneous-operation interfaces have been identified
Emergency access and escape routes remain available
Fuel, hydraulic oil and other spill risks are controlled
Breakdown / recovery arrangements avoid exposing people to moving vehicle risks
Any change to route, vehicle, load, weather or site condition will trigger reassessment

fields.label: Fuel / Oil Spill Controls and Equipment

sections.title: EXIT AND CLOSE-OUT
items: The vehicle / equipment has completed the authorised task and left or parked in the approved location
No damage, collision, spill or unsafe condition remains unreported
Temporary traffic controls have been removed or formally handed over
The work / access area is left safe for normal site operations

fields.label: Vehicle / Equipment Exit or Stand-down Date / Time
